family_summary: Across four sites, AI-built pages typically use system or sans-serif body text at 16px with slightly looser line heights (1.6–1.65) than the originals (mostly 1.5), use fewer font families, and show more varied heading and label styling, with the single-site comparisons differing in specifics like tracking, weight and hierarchy cues.

attributes.summary: AI-built pages mostly use a sans-serif body (2 of 3 sites) with one serif, whereas all 3 originals use sans-serif.
Both AI-built sites use a system-ui font stack, while the originals use named fonts (Open Sans webfonts, Helvetica Neue).
The one AI-built page uses a 16px body size versus 14px on its original.
AI-built pages all use 1.6–1.65 line height (split evenly across 4 sites), while originals mostly use 1.5 (3 of 4) with one at 2.0.
The one AI-built site uses three font families versus five on its original.
AI-built h1s use Helvetica Neue on one site and Playfair Display on the other, while originals use Open Sans and Playfair, so one serif pairing matches and the sans choice differs.
The AI-built h1 is larger and heavier (70px, weight 900) than the original (50px, weight 700) on the one site observed.

Across three single-site observations, AI-built pages vary: one uses normal tracking where the original is wide-tracked uppercase, one adds wide-tracked uppercase eyebrows where the original has only a tagline, and one swaps the original's Moontime script eyebrows for Caveat.

AI-built headings are a varied mix (uppercase with underline bar, sentence-case sans with icon, bold serif, sentence-case serif), tending toward sentence case or plain styling, while originals use more distinctive treatments such as uppercase with ticks, huge two-tone sans or lowercase letterspaced orange serif.
On the observed sites, AI-built hierarchy relies on size contrast and a date/h3/grey-excerpt card structure, whereas the originals rely on weight and color such as bold titles with blue dates.
